cues.en: There are some qualities of text that are difficult to judge using standardized tests, and that really cannot be measured using single token logits.
cues.zh: 有些文字特質，很難用標準化測驗判斷，更無法只靠單一詞元 logits 衡量。

cues.en: And these qualities of text are related to coherence and relevance, but also other qualities like helpfulness, tone, style, friendliness, and so on.
cues.zh: 包括連貫、相關，以及有幫助、語氣、風格、友善等等。

cues.en: These are the kinds of qualities in text that you know it when you see it, but it's hard to attach a number to it.
cues.zh: 這些特質，看到就知道，卻難以賦予數字。

cues.en: It's kind of like the feeling that you get when you're reading the text.
cues.zh: 有點像讀文字時的感受。

cues.en: So that's the problem.
cues.zh: 這就是問題。

cues.en: The problem is that there are qualities.
cues.zh: 文字有些特質，

cues.en: There are features of natural language that makes you like or dislike a text, but it's kind of hard to explain exactly what that means and how to quantify it.
cues.zh: 自然語言有些特徵，讓你喜歡或不喜歡，但很難精確解釋與量化。

cues.en: Let me give you an example from my own experience.
cues.zh: 用我的經驗舉例。

cues.en: I generally try to avoid social media, but I am on LinkedIn.
cues.zh: 我通常避開社群媒體，但有用 LinkedIn。

cues.en: I try not to spend too much time on LinkedIn, but there's a very specific LinkedIn writing style,
cues.zh: 也盡量不花太多時間，不過 LinkedIn 有很特定的寫作風格，

cues.en: and people use Llms to write LinkedIn style posts on LinkedIn.
cues.zh: 大家會用 LLM，寫 LinkedIn 風格的貼文。

cues.en: If you are on LinkedIn, I'm sure you know what I'm talking about.
cues.zh: 有用的人，應該知道我在說什麼。

cues.en: I find that LinkedIn style with like short, punchy sentences, lots of emojis, lots of statements that are like, it's not this, it's that.
cues.zh: 那種短而有力的句子、一堆表情符號，一直說「不是這個，而是那個」。

cues.en: I don't know exactly how to put into words what that style is, but I know it when I see it and I dislike it.
cues.zh: 我不太會用言語描述，但一看就知道，也不喜歡。

cues.en: On the other hand, it's so easy for me to just quickly scan a LinkedIn post and see if it was written
cues.zh: 另一方面，我能很快掃過貼文，看出是不是

cues.en: by a human, and then it just feels much more authentic and genuine.
cues.zh: 人寫的，感覺就真實、真誠得多。

cues.en: And then I like to engage with it, or at least give it some of my attention.
cues.zh: 接著就想互動，至少願意多看。

cues.en: Anyway, the point is that llms are designed to communicate using natural language.
cues.zh: 總之，LLM 是為了用自然語言溝通。

cues.en: Of course, there are rules governing human languages like grammar, conjugations, word order, and
cues.zh: 人類語言當然有文法、詞形變化、詞序等

cues.en: so on, but it's not nearly as constrained as like a mathematical equation.
cues.zh: 規則，但不像數學方程式那樣受限。

cues.en: There's a lot of subjectivity to natural human language, and that's all fine.
cues.zh: 自然語言有許多主觀性，這沒問題，

cues.en: It's great, but it's just really difficult to get quantitative assessments of qualities like tone and style and coherence.
cues.zh: 很好，但讓語氣、風格、連貫性的量化評估非常困難。

cues.en: Anyway, the solution to that problem is really simple.
cues.zh: 解法很簡單。

cues.en: You just have humans read text that is generated by llms, and those humans give feedback that can be
cues.zh: 讓人閱讀 LLM 生成的文字，再給回饋，

cues.en: numeric feedback, like for example, on a scale from 1 to 10, how much do you like the writing style of this piece of text?
cues.zh: 可以是數字，例如 1 到 10 分，有多喜歡這段寫作風格？

cues.en: The feedback can also be in the form of choosing one of two texts that the Raiders prefer.
cues.zh: 也可以讓評分者從兩段文字選偏好的一段。

cues.en: Or it can be reading two texts and trying to determine which one was generated by a model and which was written by a human.
cues.zh: 或讀兩段，判斷哪個是模型生成、哪個是人寫的。

cues.en: I've already discussed this kind of feedback, like human in the loop feedback.
cues.zh: 前面介紹人類回饋強化學習時，

cues.en: Earlier in the course when I introduced you to reinforcement learning from human feedback.
cues.zh: 已談過這種人類參與迴圈的回饋。

cues.en: On the other hand, people have different preferences for what kinds of writing styles they like.
cues.zh: 但大家喜歡的寫作風格不同。

cues.en: So these kinds of human ratings can be important and insightful, but are also subjective and can be variable and noisy.
cues.zh: 所以評分重要、有洞見，卻也主觀、變異大、有雜訊。

cues.en: Nonetheless, getting real humans to evaluate model output is a big component of qualitative evaluations of LL.
cues.zh: 不過，請真人評估輸出，仍是 LLM 質性評估的重要部分。

cues.en: In fact, there are companies that you can hire that will run these kinds of human evaluations for you.
cues.zh: 甚至能聘公司，替你執行這些評估。

cues.en: And this screenshot here shows just one example company.
cues.zh: 截圖只是一家公司的例子。

cues.en: And just to be super clear, I am not affiliated with this company.
cues.zh: 說清楚，我與這家公司無關，

cues.en: I'm not specifically endorsing them.
cues.zh: 沒有特別背書，

cues.en: I'm not telling you that you should use this company or their services and not any other company.
cues.zh: 也不是要你選它，而不要其他公司。

cues.en: This is just one example of many companies out there that provide these kinds of services.
cues.zh: 只是許多提供這類人評服務的公司之一。

cues.en: If you want to have a model evaluated by humans, I wonder what you think of all this.
cues.zh: 如果想讓人評模型，可以考慮。也好奇你怎麼看。

cues.en: Maybe you are thinking that the frontier models are now so good and so humanlike that maybe we don't even need the human ratings at all.
cues.zh: 也許你想，前沿模型已很強、很像人，根本不再需要真人評分。

cues.en: Maybe the quote unquote human ratings can actually be generated by a frontier, like the latest version of OpenAI's GPT.
cues.zh: 所謂人類評分，能否由最新 OpenAI GPT 等前沿模型生成？

cues.en: In fact, that is also possible.
cues.zh: 確實可以。

cues.en: You can have human like judgments done by other capable GMs, and that's probably fine for like fine
cues.zh: 可以讓其他強大 LLM 做類人判斷，用來微調，

cues.en: tuning and maybe some instruction tuning of newly developed models.
cues.zh: 或替新模型做一些指令微調，也許可以。

cues.en: But I admit that I am a little bit skeptical of the quality that you can achieve when you're having
cues.zh: 但我承認，有點懷疑這種品質，

cues.en: like, awkward language models evaluate the naturalness and flow and human like texture and flavor of human written language.
cues.zh: 讓生硬的語言模型，評估其他模型生成文字的自然度、流暢度、

cues.en: In other models generating tokens.
cues.zh: 以及近似人類文字的質感與韻味。

cues.en: That said, it is technically fairly straightforward and is similar to generative adversarial models,
cues.zh: 不過，技術上相當直接，也類似生成對抗模型，

cues.en: which you might have learned about, for example, if you studied image generation in deep learning.
cues.zh: 如果學過深度學習生圖，可能知道。

cues.en: So that's it for this video.
cues.zh: 這支就到這裡。

cues.en: The main point is that there are certain features or qualities of text that are hard to describe quantitatively
cues.zh: 重點是，某些文字特徵難以量化描述，

cues.en: and are therefore difficult to automate, but are still used to assess the quality and coherence of language model outputs.
cues.zh: 因此難自動化，但仍被用於評估輸出品質與連貫性。
